title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
seo_title: Grade 10 Science (SNC2D): Chemical Reactions and Equations Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Naming and writing formulas for ionic and molecular compounds; word, skeleton and balanced chemical equations; the law of conservation of mass; and the four main types of reaction: synthesis, decomposition, single displacement and double displacement. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 9 and 10: Science (2008), Science, Grade 10, Academic (SNC2D), Strand C: Chemical Reactions)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science (SNC2D) worksheets on chemical reactions: naming compounds, writing formulas, word and skeleton equations, balancing equations, conservation of mass and types of reactions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mass is conserved: the atoms on each side of an equation must match.
key_sub: Synthesis, decomposition, single and double displacement.
body_html:
How to think about it

Name ionic compounds metal first, then the non-metal ending in -ide (sodium chloride, NaCl). Cross the ion charges to write formulas (Al³⁺ and O²⁻ give Al₂O₃). Molecular compounds use prefixes: carbon dioxide (CO₂), dinitrogen tetroxide (N₂O₄).

A word equation names the substances; a skeleton equation uses formulas; a balanced equation adds coefficients so atoms are conserved. The four types are synthesis (A + B → AB), decomposition (AB → A + B), single displacement (A + BC → AC + B) and double displacement (AB + CD → AD + CB).

Example

Formula of calcium chloride?

Ca²⁺ and Cl⁻

Two Cl⁻ for each Ca²⁺

Answer: CaCl₂

Example

Balance: Na + Cl₂ → NaCl

2 Cl on the left, so 2 NaCl

Then 2 Na

Answer: 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl

Common mistakes

  • Using prefixes for ionic compounds (it is calcium chloride, not calcium dichloride).
  • Changing subscripts to balance an equation.
  • Forgetting that oxygen, hydrogen and chlorine gases are diatomic.

faq.q: What is the law of conservation of mass?
faq.a: In a chemical reaction the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.

faq.q: Why does a burning candle seem to lose mass?
faq.a: Gases (carbon dioxide and water vapour) escape into the air; in a closed container the mass stays the same.

items.q: What is the formula of sodium chloride?
items.e: Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is NaCl.

items.q: What is the name of CaF<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: What is the formula of calcium oxide?
items.e: Ca<sup>2+</sup> and O<sup>2−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is CaO.

items.q: Na<sup>+</sup> and O<sup>2−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 2 × (+1) + 1 × (−2) = 0.

items.q: Chloe writes this equation for methane burning: 2CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. Is it balanced?
c: Yes, because both sides have the same substances.
No. The number of some atoms is different on each side.
items.e: Count each kind of atom on both sides; at least one does not match.

items.q: How many atoms of S are in 2SO<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: 2SO<sub>3</sub>: the coefficient 2 multiplies every atom in the formula, so 2 × 1 = 2.

items.q: Mateo checks the equation for magnesium burning: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. Is it balanced?
c: No. The products have more atoms.
Balance does not matter in reactions.
Yes. Each kind of atom has the same number on both sides.
No. The reactants have more atoms.
items.e: Atoms are only rearranged, so the counts match.

items.q:
Which type of chemical change is shown by this word equation?
sulfuric acid + potassium hydroxide → potassium sulfate + water
items.e: An acid and an alkali make a salt and water.

items.q:

items.q: Magnesium reacts with oxygen gas. What is the formula of the product?

items.q:
Mass
lemon juice80 g
baking soda21 g
total after reaction101 g
Ethan mixed lemon juice and baking soda inside a sealed bag. Gas formed. What does the data show?
c: Mass was created by the reaction.
Mass was conserved because no matter could escape.
Mass was lost because a gas formed.
items.e: 80 + 21 = 101 g before and after.

items.q: A 60 g solution is mixed with a 10 g solution in a sealed flask and a solid forms. What is the total mass now?
items.e: No atoms escape a sealed flask, so the mass stays the same.

items.q: A 120 g solution is mixed with a 20 g solution in a sealed flask and a solid forms. What is the total mass now?
items.e: No atoms escape a sealed flask, so the mass stays the same.

items.q:
Mass
an antacid tablet33 g
water30 g
total after reaction57 g
Ava mixed an antacid tablet and water in an open cup. Gas bubbled out. Why is the total mass after the reaction 6 g less?
c: The gas escaped into the air, but the atoms were not destroyed.
Atoms were destroyed in the reaction.
items.e: In an open system, gas leaves the cup. In a sealed bag, the mass would stay the same.

items.q: Ethan reacts 6 g of carbon with 16 g of oxygen. Both are used up. What mass of carbon dioxide forms?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 6 + 16 = 22 g.

items.q: Emma reacts 21 g of magnesium with 14 g of oxygen. Both are used up. What mass of magnesium oxide forms?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 21 + 14 = 35 g.

items.q: Noah puts 30 g of marble chips and acid in an open flask. After the reaction it has a mass of 27 g. Why is it lighter?
c: Mass is not conserved in reactions.
Carbon dioxide gas escaped into the air.
items.e: The gas leaves the open flask: 3 g of it.

items.q: Marble chips react with acid in an open beaker on a balance. The mass shown goes down from 60 g to 58 g. Why?
c: Carbon dioxide gas escapes into the air.
Mass is destroyed in the reaction.
items.e: Mass is conserved; the gas leaves the beaker.

items.q: 25 g of calcium carbonate is heated and breaks down. 11 g of carbon dioxide escapes. What mass of calcium oxide is left?
items.e: Mass of products = mass of reactant: 25 − 11 = 14 g.

items.q: 24 g of magnesium burns in air and joins with 16 g of oxygen. What mass of magnesium oxide forms?
items.e: The magnesium gains the mass of the oxygen: 24 + 16.

items.q: Ava mixes 25 g of one solution with 15 g of another in a sealed flask. A precipitate forms. What is the total mass after the reaction?
items.e: Mass is conserved: no atoms are created or destroyed.

Zoe reacts 6 g of magnesium with 4 g of oxygen. Both are used up. What mass of magnesium oxide forms?
